title: Derived tower evaluation with its unit and counit normalization
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and $F:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ additive functors with $F\dashv G$ and $F$ exact. Assume their strict inverse-sequence categories are also Grothendieck abelian, with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], termwise functors $F^{\rm Tow},G^{\rm Tow}$ and exact evaluations $e_n$. Compute $\mathcal G=RG$ and $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}=R(G^{\rm Tow})$ by K-injectives [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], with universal units $\eta_G,\eta_{G^{\rm Tow}}$. For every $n$ there is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\beta_n:e_n\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G e_n$$
normalized as follows. For a K-injective tower complex $J$, under ordinary $e_nG^{\rm Tow}=Ge_n$ and localization/evaluation identifications,
$$\beta_{n,QJ}\circ e_n(\eta_{G^{\rm Tow},J})=\eta_{G,e_nJ}.$$
These comparisons commute with every tower transition. They also carry evaluation of the canonical derived tower adjunction counit to the ambient derived counit: for every $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$,
$$e_n(\varepsilon^{\rm Tow}_M)=\varepsilon_{e_nM}\circ F(\beta_{n,M}),$$
using $e_nF^{\rm Tow}=Fe_n$. Thus evaluation of the derived tower adjunction is the specified ambient adjunction, including its counit.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim: evaluation in its diagram-topos proof, expanded by K-injective derived-pair uniqueness

proof.text: Write $Q$ for each localization, suppressing its exact-functor comparison isomorphisms. The ordinary tower adjunction $F^{\rm Tow}\dashv G^{\rm Tow}$ is defined by applying the ordinary Hom bijection at each level: naturality of that bijection says exactly that compatible level maps correspond to compatible level maps. Its unit and counit are levelwise the original ones. Levelwise exactness makes $F^{\rm Tow}$ exact, and evaluations and $F,F^{\rm Tow}$ therefore induce termwise exact derived functors. The additive adjunctions also induce adjunctions on homotopy categories. These identifications retain the ordinary units and counits, not arbitrary adjunctions with the same functors.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; termwise adjunction of Tag 0DVC, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors

proof.text: The assumed Grothendieck property gives K-injective resolutions in $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ and both tower categories. For a K-injective tower complex $J$ in $\mathcal A$, evaluation preserves K-injectivity, so $e_nJ$ is K-injective. The total-derived computation theorem makes both $a_n(J):=e_n(\eta_{G^{\rm Tow},J})$ and $b_n(J):=\eta_{G,e_nJ}$ invertible. Both have source $Q(G(e_nJ))$, by the strict ordinary evaluation identity. Put $A_n=e_n\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}$ and $B_n=\mathcal G e_n$ and define $\delta_n(J)=b_n(J)a_n(J)^{-1}:A_n(QJ)\to B_n(QJ)$. Thus $\delta_n(J)a_n(J)=b_n(J)$, the required normalization.

source.place: Tags 070K and 070Y, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies and lemma-K-injective-defined; existence: injectives.tex Tag 079P

proof.text:
For a homotopy class $k:J\to J'$ between K-injective tower complexes, naturality of the two universal derived units gives
$$A_n(Qk)a_n(J)=a_n(J')Q(G(e_nk)),\qquad B_n(Qk)b_n(J)=b_n(J')Q(G(e_nk)).$$
Substituting $\delta_n= b_na_n^{-1}$ yields $B_n(Qk)\delta_n(J)=\delta_n(J')A_n(Qk)$. Additive functors respect homotopies, so this calculation uses the homotopy class of $k$. It proves naturality on the full subcategory of K-injective complexes in the homotopy category.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined: naturality of the derived comparison; Tag 0DVC, termwise functors on homotopy categories

proof.text:
For each $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ choose an isomorphism $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$ with $J$ K-injective, using a representative of $M$ and a K-injective resolution. Define
$$\beta_{n,M}=B_n(u)^{-1}\delta_n(J)A_n(u).$$
For another choice $u':M\to QJ'$, full faithfulness of localization on K-injectives gives a unique homotopy class $k:J\to J'$ with $Qk=u'u^{-1}$. Step 3, multiplied by $B_n(u')^{-1}$ on the left and $A_n(u)$ on the right, proves that the two definitions coincide. For any $h:M\to N$ and choices $u:M\to QJ$, $v:N\to QJ'$, use the unique class $k$ with $Qk=vhu^{-1}$ in the same equation; it gives $B_n(h)\beta_{n,M}=\beta_{n,N}A_n(h)$. Thus $\beta_n$ is a natural isomorphism. Taking $u=1$ proves its normalization. Any normalized comparison equals $\delta_n$ at $QJ$ by cancellation of $a_n(J)$; naturality with respect to $u$ forces the displayed formula at $M$. This proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, fully faithful localization on K-injectives; injectives.tex Tag 079P

proof.text:
Fix a tower transition $t:e_m\to e_n$ ($m\geq n$). Denote the induced transitions $A_m\to A_n$ and $B_m\to B_n$ by $s_A,s_B$. At $QJ$, naturality of evaluation transitions with respect to the tower morphism $\eta_{G^{\rm Tow},J}$ and naturality of $\eta_G$ with respect to $t_J:e_mJ\to e_nJ$ give
$$s_Aa_m=a_nQ(Gt_J),\qquad s_Bb_m=b_nQ(Gt_J).$$
Consequently $s_B\delta_m a_m=b_nQ(Gt_J)=\delta_n s_Aa_m$. Cancel the invertible $a_m$. This is transition compatibility at $QJ$; conjugating by the functorial images of $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$ proves it at every $M$. The calculation applies to every transition, including identity transitions.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined: naturality of universal units, applied also to tower transition maps

proof.text:
Apply the normalized derived-adjunction theorem to $F\dashv G$ and $F^{\rm Tow}\dashv G^{\rm Tow}$, using all source homotopy objects as the left resolving class. Identity resolutions verify the resolving condition; exactness of the left functors ensures that their localized termwise functors invert quasi-isomorphisms. K-injective resolutions give the right derived pairs. The theorem's Hom-transpose formula specifies the canonical adjunctions. Write $\varepsilon^0$ for the ordinary counits and $\varepsilon^D$ for these derived counits. For a K-injective target $I$, apply that formula to the ordinary map $\varepsilon^0_I:F(GI)\to I$. Its ordinary transpose is $1_{GI}$, so its derived transpose is $\eta_{G,I}$. By the definition of an adjunction counit as inverse transpose of the identity, the inverse transpose of $\eta_{G,I}$ is $\varepsilon^D_{QI}F(\eta_{G,I})$. Therefore
$$\varepsilon^D_{QI}F(\eta_{G,I})=Q(\varepsilon^0_I).$$
The same argument in the tower categories gives $\varepsilon^{D,\rm Tow}_{QJ}F^{\rm Tow}(\eta_{G^{\rm Tow},J})=Q(\varepsilon^{0,\rm Tow}_J)$. All the exact-localization identifications are those of step 1.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors, with the normalized Hom formula of the cited resolving-class theorem

proof.text:
At a K-injective tower $J$, evaluate the tower counit equation of step 6. Since the ordinary tower counit is levelwise the ambient one, it reads
$$e_n(\varepsilon^{D,\rm Tow}_{QJ})F(a_n(J))=Q(\varepsilon^0_{e_nJ}).$$
For the proposed right-hand side of the claimed identity, normalization of $\beta_n$ and the ambient equation of step 6 give
$$\varepsilon^D_{e_nQJ}F(\beta_{n,QJ})F(a_n(J))=\varepsilon^D_{e_nQJ}F(b_n(J))=Q(\varepsilon^0_{e_nJ}).$$
Here $e_nJ$ is K-injective, as established in step 2. Cancel the isomorphism $F(a_n(J))$. This proves the required counit equality at $QJ$.

source.place: Tag 09T5, lemma-derived-adjoint-functors: compare the two normalized counits on a K-injective representative

proof.text: Let $C(M)=e_n(\varepsilon^{D,\rm Tow}_M)$ and $D(M)=\varepsilon^D_{e_nM}F(\beta_{n,M})$. They are natural transformations $F A_n\to e_n$, by naturality of the counits and step 4. For $u:M\xrightarrow{\sim}QJ$, naturality gives $e_n(u)C(M)=C(QJ)F A_n(u)$ and $e_n(u)D(M)=D(QJ)F A_n(u)$. Step 7 identifies the right sides; cancel $e_n(u)$ to obtain $C(M)=D(M)$. Thus the normalized comparisons have the stated counit compatibility for every derived tower object.

The delivery is one commit and creates no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from the base, and there is no re-split note for this item. Sources: Stacks 0A07 (sites-cohomology.tex:5150, diagram-topos proof) and the first sentence of the main-20261015 proof of prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits; the proof is correctly marked by: agent. All step tags (015F, 070Y, 070I, 070K, 09T5, 0DVC, 079P) match tags/tags, and no SGA is cited. Steps 2-4: δ=b·a⁻¹ is well defined because e_nJ is K-injective by lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective and η is invertible on K-injectives by kinjective-total-derived. Naturality holds on K-injective towers. Descent to all M works because u'u⁻¹=Qk with k unique (kinjective-hom-derived), and uniqueness follows by cancelling a(J). Step 5: I checked the transition equations s_A a_m=a_n QG(t_J) and s_B b_m=b_n QG(t_J); no epimorphic transitions are used. Step 6: lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization applies with the roles swapped (its G=F, its F=G), with P = all objects; taking f=ε⁰_I gives ε^D F(η_{G,I})=Q(ε⁰_I), and that Hom formula determines the adjunction uniquely. Steps 7-8: the counit equation holds on K-injectives and extends to all M by naturality along u:M≅QJ, not by joint faithfulness of the evaluations. Edge cases checked: zero objects, F=G=id (β is the identity), zero and identity transitions. No cycle: none of the cited closures reaches the item. A DAG grep found no duplicate. The declared tool use of lem-sfb-resolving-derived-adjunction-normalization is accepted. Three minor points, not faults: (1) exactness of the termwise QG on K(A) is used without a cited node, which is standard; (2) step 6 does not say explicitly that (F_D, φ⁻¹) is the universal left derived pair; (3) lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence comes from another unit (sk-prop-cd) and is not declared as a tool use, which other pbc nodes also leave undeclared; the maintainer should record it at the merge.
